_**Agent (default)**_

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
I'll build a lightweight i18n system to localize the site in French and add a language switcher.

I'll create five files: locale types, English and French dictionaries, a provider with hooks, and a language switcher component. Page metadata will adapt to the active locale. Email labels will remain in English for the site owner.

The i18n dictionaries will use nested objects with strict TypeScript typing. A `Locale` union and a `Record` mapping both languages to their dictionaries will enforce structural parity between English and French.

The translation function will support dot-notation access like `t.nav.skills` instead of string keys. The provider will expose `locale`, `setLocale`, and `t`. The loading screen will read the preferred locale from localStorage before rendering.

Browser language detection will default to French if the navigator locale starts with "fr", otherwise English, and persist the choice to localStorage. The language switcher will use a monospaced font with EN and FR toggles, highlighting the active selection in the primary color. On mobile, it will sit beside the call-to-action button; on desktop, it will sit beside the navigation links. The onboarding shell will also place the switcher next to the step counter. Month abbreviations in experience periods will be translated into French equivalents.

Brand roles and skill category titles will be translated. Technical skill names will remain in English. Code-style section headings will be translated into French while keeping file-name prefixes unchanged.

SEO schema will react to locale changes via useLocale. usePageMeta will pull locale-aware metadata from the dictionaries. Translatable SEO strings will move out of siteConfig and into i18n, while non-translatable defaults stay in seo.ts.

Pages will pass translated metadata directly into `usePageMeta` using the locale hook. The provider will also set `document.documentElement.lang` dynamically. LoadingScreen lines will be pulled from the active locale, though mounting before the locale is resolved may complicate that.
</details></think>

_**Agent (default)**_

French localization is live with an **EN | FR** switcher.

### What you get
- Lightweight i18n (`LocaleProvider` + `en`/`fr` dictionaries) — no heavy library
- Preference saved in `localStorage`, with French auto-detected from the browser
- Switcher in the **navbar** (mobile + desktop) and **onboarding** header
- Home, project form, 404, loading screen, and SEO/meta/schema all translated

### How to try it
Toggle **EN | FR** in the top-right. Refresh to confirm the choice sticks.

Inquiry emails still use English labels in your inbox so they’re consistent for you.
